svg.text: THE HOME VISIT — YOU ARE A GUEST, NOT AN INSPECTOR

g.text: Agree the time; the household is not on call
Review the record and set an aim for the visit
Pack the bag: gloves, apron, hand rub, sharps box
Take a clean surface to put the bag on
Tell a colleague where you are going
Plan how waste and sharps come back with you
Greet the household properly and ask permission
Sit at the person's level; do not stand over them
Ask what they want from the visit first
Work with what the home has, not what you wish
it had — improvise safely, never unsafely
Teach the carer by doing it together, not for them

svg.text: WHAT THE HOME TELLS YOU THAT THE CLINIC NEVER WILL

g.text: Is there food in the house, and who cooks it?
Where is the water, and who fetches it?
How far is the latrine, and is the path safe at night?
Gather every medicine in the house into one place
Who actually gives the tablets, and how do they know?
Who is the carer, and who is caring for the carer?
Leave written or picture instructions that match
what the family can actually read
Agree exactly what to do if things get worse,
and where to go at night
Set the date of the next visit before you go
Record the visit the same day, while it is fresh
